{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when assessed by Time-to-Target, Success rate, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation produced the highest success rate (0.780) and fastest Time-to-Target (2.562 s), with high Path Efficiency (0.502) and Average Speed (12.83 units/s), and the highest AD (0.399) indicating more angular dispersion in trajectories.",
    "Bright Visual Only showed strong performance with success rate 0.785, Time-to-Target 2.614 s, Path Efficiency 0.504, and Speed 12.68 units/s, with AD of 0.387.",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only performed similarly and intermediately: Dim Visual had success 0.673, Time-to-Target 3.140 s, Path Efficiency 0.434, Speed 11.97 units/s, AD 0.336; ICMS Only had success 0.685, Time-to-Target 3.053 s, Path Efficiency 0.432, Speed 12.04 units/s, AD 0.354.",
    "Sham stimulation showed dramatically impaired performance: lowest success rate (0.273), slowest Time-to-Target (4.682 s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), slowest Average Speed (10.74 units/s), and lowest AD (0.236).",
    "Across all paradigms, Success and Time-to-Target showed the largest dynamic ranges (0.273 to 0.785 for success; 2.56 to 4.68 s for time), while Path Efficiency and AD showed substantial variation (0.308 to 0.504 for efficiency; 0.236 to 0.399 for AD).",
    "AD (angular dispersion) was highest in Combined and Bright Visual conditions and lowest in Sham, suggesting that active stimulation conditions permit or produce more variable, exploratory, or less direct trajectories compared to the Sham condition."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Sham vs. all active stimulation paradigms: Sham success rate (0.273) was less than half that of Combined (0.780) and Bright Visual (0.785), representing a 2.9-fold difference.",
    "Sham vs. Combined in Time-to-Target: Sham was 1.83× slower (4.68 s vs. 2.56 s).",
    "Sham vs. Combined in Path Efficiency: Sham was 1.63× lower (0.308 vs. 0.502).",
    "Sham vs. Combined in AD: Sham showed 1.69× lower angular dispersion (0.236 vs. 0.399), suggesting Sham trajectories were more stereotyped or direct despite being less efficient.",
    "Dim Visual Only vs. Bright Visual Only: Bright Visual showed 0.112 higher success rate (0.785 vs. 0.673), 0.527 s faster Time-to-Target, and 0.069 higher Path Efficiency, indicating that stimulus intensity matters for visual-only stimulation.",
    "Combined vs. single-modality conditions: Combined outperformed both Dim Visual and ICMS Only on all metrics except AD, where it was slightly higher (more dispersed) than Bright Visual."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "The data support a clear hierarchy of navigation performance: Combined and Bright Visual stimulation yield the best outcomes, single-modality stimulation (ICMS or Dim Visual) produces intermediate performance, and Sham stimulation results in severely impaired navigation. The high AD values in successful conditions (Combined, Bright Visual) combined with high path efficiency suggests that mice can afford more exploratory, angularly dispersed trajectories when they have reliable sensory information, whereas in Sham conditions, low AD coupled with low path efficiency indicates stereotyped, ineffective movement patterns. The substantial Sham deficit confirms that the stimulation paradigms are not merely additive but necessary for normal task performance in this navigation task. For practical applications, Combined stimulation offers minimal advantage over Bright Visual Only for most metrics, suggesting that visual information may be the dominant driver of performance in this task, though the sample size imbalance (Combined n=48,846 vs. Bright Visual n=3,323) limits certainty about this comparison.",
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in sample sizes across paradigms: Combined has 48,846 trials while Bright Visual Only has only 3,323 and Sham has 3,505, which affects the precision of comparisons and may introduce selection or historical confounds.",
    "No statistical tests (e.g., ANOVA, mixed models) are provided; all comparisons are descriptive and effect sizes are not formally estimated with confidence intervals.",
    "Individual mouse effects are present in the data (8 mice with varying performance levels) but not statistically separated from paradigm effects in this analysis; some paradigms may be confounded with specific mice or testing periods.",
    "The AD metric interpretation as 'angular dispersion' is assumed from the prompt but not operationally defined in the data artifacts; the relationship between AD and trajectory characteristics remains descriptive.",
    "Success is binary (0/1) but treated descriptively as a proportion without modeling approaches appropriate for binary outcomes.",
    "No information about trial sequence, learning effects, or temporal dynamics is available in the provided artifacts."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects model with Mouse as a random effect and Stim Paradigm as a fixed effect to obtain paradigm-specific estimates adjusted for individual mouse performance differences, with appropriate confidence intervals and significance testing. Additionally, compute Cohen's d or standardized mean differences for key pairwise comparisons (especially Sham vs. each active condition and Combined vs. Bright Visual Only) to quantify effect sizes independent of sample size. Finally, explore the relationship between AD and Path Efficiency within each paradigm using correlation analysis to test whether higher angular dispersion is associated with more efficient paths (suggesting strategic exploration) or less efficient paths (suggesting disorientation)."
